clusters.summary: Calling IsValid inside CommandResponseFromJSON turns the previously lenient integration decoder into a hard gate, so payloads that were tolerated before (unrecognized or differently-cased response_type, oversized ephemeral text) now fail the whole command with a 500/400 and lose all sibling content, an unannounced compatibility break with no config gate or deprecation.
clusters.rationale: Calling IsValid inside the decoder turns previously tolerated payloads into hard failures at both ingest sites (500 in DoCommandRequest, 400 in commandWebhook) with no config gate — the same compatibility-break concern the human thread raised when asking for a logged warning instead of an error.

clusters.summary: The two new AppError i18n IDs (model.command_response.is_valid.response_type.app_error and .text.app_error) are missing from server/i18n/en.json, so the raw dotted key becomes the error Message in logs, developer-mode responses and Go client errors.
clusters.rationale: grep of server/i18n/en.json finds no model.command_response.is_valid.* entries, so the raw id becomes the translated message; this is the human thread's request to run i18n-extract for the new error ids.

clusters.summary: The text-length check compares len(o.Text) bytes against a hardcoded 65535 while the governing post limit is a configurable rune count (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 / determineMaxPostSize), so the two limits neither agree nor nest — CJK text is rejected that would fit, ASCII passes that fails downstream, and enlarged-column installs get a new fixed ceiling.
clusters.rationale: len(o.Text) counts bytes against a hardcoded 65535 while Post.IsValid enforces a configurable rune count (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 / determineMaxPostSize), which is exactly the byte-vs-character concern the human thread raised.

clusters.summary: CommandResponseFromHTTPBody only validates the application/json branch; text/plain bodies go through CommandResponseFromPlainText which never calls IsValid, so the same oversized payload is rejected as JSON but accepted by switching Content-Type.
clusters.rationale: CommandResponseFromPlainText never calls IsValid, so the text-length rule applies only to application/json bodies; a real inconsistency in the new validation, though the length is re-checked at post creation so practical impact is small.

clusters.summary: Unbounded recursion of IsValid over ExtraResponses (deep nesting or a cyclic value) as a stack-exhaustion vector — examined and cleared because encoding/json's nesting cap, the 1 MB LimitReader and Go's growable stack bound it and JSON cannot construct a cycle.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared stack-exhaustion note; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: A typed-nil *AppError from IsValid could escape as a non-nil error interface at the CommandResponseFromJSON call site — examined and cleared because the concrete pointer is nil-tested before conversion.
clusters.rationale: Cleared note: the *AppError is nil-tested as a concrete pointer before being returned as error, so no typed-nil escape.

clusters.summary: StringifyMessageAttachmentFieldValue is applied only one level deep in CommandResponseFromJSON, so attachments in nested ExtraResponses are never stringified while IsValid now recurses fully (pre-existing asymmetry).
clusters.rationale: The asymmetry is real (stringification is one level deep, IsValid recurses), but nested ExtraResponses beyond one level are never consumed by HandleCommandResponse, so nothing observable follows.

clusters.summary: maxLength := 65535 is a function-local magic number rather than a package-level constant (or a reference to the existing PostMessageMaxBytesV2), unlike the file's other constants.
clusters.rationale: 65535 is a function-local literal that duplicates PostMessageMaxBytesV2 rather than referencing it or a package constant, unlike the file's other constants; correct and actionable but small.

clusters.summary: The comment `// check response type` merely restates the following condition and gives no rationale for the allowlist or why the empty string is accepted.
clusters.rationale: The comment restates the condition; purely stylistic, no defect.

clusters.summary: The new extra_responses test case is indented with spaces while sibling table cases use tabs.
clusters.rationale: Space indentation inside a raw string literal in one test case; purely cosmetic and untouched by gofmt.

clusters.summary: Validation lives in the shared bidirectional decoder CommandResponseFromJSON, which Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam also use to decode server-emitted responses that are never validated server-side (plugin/built-in commands), so a response the webapp renders fine fails to decode in mmctl and every Go client; validation belongs at the ingest sites, not the decoder.
clusters.rationale: CommandResponseFromJSON is also the decoder used by Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam for server-emitted responses that are never run through IsValid server-side, so placing validation in the shared decoder is misplaced; the human thread asks for the same relocation of the call to commandWebhook/DoCommandRequest, albeit motivated by logger context rather than client breakage.

clusters.summary: The recursive IsValid call returns a nested ExtraResponses failure verbatim, so the error carries no index or path and is indistinguishable from a top-level failure.
clusters.rationale: The nested error is returned verbatim with no index or path, so an integration author cannot tell which extra_responses entry failed; small debuggability gap.

clusters.summary: The new test cases assert only assert.Error/assert.Nil (with an ASCII payload that does not pin byte vs rune) and never check the AppError Id or StatusCode, so a case failing for an unrelated reason such as a JSON typo still passes.
clusters.rationale: The new ShouldError cases only assert.Error/assert.Nil and never check the AppError Id or StatusCode, so a case failing for an unrelated reason would still pass, and the ASCII payload cannot distinguish byte from rune counting; correct, actionable test-strength nit.

clusters.summary: CommandResponseFromHTTPBody returns (nil, nil) when io.ReadAll fails, swallowing the read error and forcing callers into a separate nil check (pre-existing).
clusters.rationale: When io.ReadAll fails the function returns (nil, nil), discarding the error and forcing callers into a separate nil check that reports a generic 'empty response'; true but pre-existing and outside the changed hunk.

clusters.summary: IsValid recurses through all ExtraResponses and propagates any nested failure, so one bad extra entry (even at a depth no consumer ever reads) rejects the whole payload and discards the valid main message, contradicting HandleCommandResponse's per-entry tolerance.
clusters.rationale: One invalid nested entry (even at depth 2, which HandleCommandResponse never reads) rejects the entire payload with a hard error, contrasting with HandleCommandResponse's per-entry continue-and-log; this is a facet of the human thread's objection to hard-erroring instead of logging a warning.

clusters.summary: The len(o.Text) > maxLength boundary was checked for an off-by-one against the 65536-byte test and found exact.
clusters.rationale: A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect (the > 65535 vs 65536-byte test is indeed exact).

clusters.summary: The response_type allowlist (in_channel, ephemeral, empty) might be too narrow — examined and cleared since no other legitimate values were found in built-in commands, plugins or docs.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note asserting the allowlist is fine; no defect claimed.

clusters.summary: The http.StatusBadRequest set on IsValid's AppErrors has no observable effect because both call sites wrap it in a fresh outer AppError, so the failure surfaces to the user as a generic 500 via app/command.go.
clusters.rationale: Accurate that both server call sites wrap the AppError in a fresh outer error with their own fixed status (500 / 400) and Client4 wraps in fmt.Errorf, but this is the existing convention for every model IsValid and offers no clear action for this change.

clusters.summary: An empty-string ResponseType is accepted by IsValid — examined and cleared as required for consistency with the plain-text path and empty-means-ephemeral handling.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note that empty ResponseType is intentionally accepted; no defect.

clusters.summary: commandWebhook reads r.Body without a LimitReader, unlike the outgoing-command path capped at MaxIntegrationResponseSize (pre-existing).
clusters.rationale: commandWebhook is served through web.Handler which wraps r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader(MaximumPayloadSizeBytes) before the handler runs, so the body is already bounded; the implied unbounded-read concern does not hold (and is pre-existing regardless).

clusters.summary: The newly exported IsValid has no nil-receiver guard — cleared because call sites are non-nil and sibling IsValid methods omit it too.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared nil-receiver note; sibling IsValid methods omit the guard too.

clusters.summary: err is shadowed at the IsValid call in CommandResponseFromJSON — idiomatic Go, not a bug.
clusters.rationale: Self-described as not a bug; idiomatic if-scoped err.

clusters.summary: The test literal "shliapa_type" used as an invalid response_type is inert test data, not a defect.
clusters.rationale: Explicitly asserts no defect; test-data naming.

clusters.summary: ExpectedCommandResponse: nil is never asserted for ShouldError table rows — a pre-existing table convention.
clusters.rationale: Notes a pre-existing table convention without asserting a defect.

clusters.summary: The `if resp == nil { continue }` branch of IsValid (and the nested text-length branch) has no test coverage — no test puts a null element in extra_responses.
clusters.rationale: No table case puts a null element in extra_responses, so the nil-skip branch of IsValid (and the nested text-length branch) is exercised only by construction; a small but correct coverage gap.

clusters.summary: IsValid's nil-skip lets {"extra_responses":[null]} through as a nil element that HandleCommandResponse/HandleCommandResponsePost later dereference, a reachable nil-pointer panic from commandWebhook and custom slash commands.
clusters.rationale: IsValid explicitly skips nil ExtraResponses entries, and HandleCommandResponse passes each entry to HandleCommandResponsePost which dereferences response.Type without a nil check, so {"extra_responses":[null]} from a custom command or command webhook reaches a nil-pointer panic; pre-existing, but the new validation is the natural place to reject it.

clusters.summary: The tests use 65536 (rejected) but never pin that exactly 65535 passes, so a > to >= regression at the boundary would go unnoticed.
clusters.rationale: Only the 65536-byte rejection is tested; nothing pins that exactly 65535 bytes passes, so a >= regression would go unnoticed.

clusters.summary: No green-path test asserts that response_type "in_channel" alone is accepted — the only in_channel cases both expect errors.
clusters.rationale: The only in_channel cases in TestCommandResponseFromJSON both expect errors; there is no success case pinning that in_channel is accepted by the new allowlist.

clusters.summary: IsValid is new exported public API with no direct unit test; it is exercised only transitively through CommandResponseFromJSON.
clusters.rationale: There is no TestCommandResponseIsValid; the exported method is only exercised through CommandResponseFromJSON, a small coverage/structure nit.

clusters.summary: TestCommandResponseFromHTTPBody is untouched, so the text/plain bypass of the new validation is not pinned in either direction by a test.
clusters.rationale: TestCommandResponseFromHTTPBody has no case for an oversized or invalid text/plain body, so the plain-text path's non-validation is unpinned; a small test suggestion.

clusters.summary: The newly exported IsValid has no doc comment stating what it validates.
clusters.rationale: Sibling IsValid methods in the model package (Post, Command) also lack doc comments; stylistic preference, not a defect.

clusters.summary: The DetailedError strings ("invalid response type", "text is too long") omit the offending value and actual/max length, unlike Post.IsValid, making the rejection hard to debug for integration authors.
clusters.rationale: DetailedError strings carry no offending value or actual/max length, unlike Post.IsValid which passes Length/MaxLength params; small debuggability nit.

clusters.summary: For a change billed as strict validation, IsValid leaves ChannelId, Type (system_ prefix), Username, IconURL, Props and Attachments unvalidated — narrower scope than the commit message implies.
clusters.rationale: IsValid checks only ResponseType, Text length and recursion; ChannelId, Type, Username, IconURL, Props and Attachments (which have their own MessageAttachment.IsValid) are untouched, so the scope observation is accurate though largely a design/scope remark.

clusters.summary: server/Makefile's i18n-check target does not run `mmgotool i18n check`, so CI cannot catch missing en.json keys like the ones this change introduces.
clusters.rationale: True that i18n-check omits `mmgotool i18n check`, but this is a repository-tooling observation outside the change under review rather than a defect in the PR; borderline, since it explains why the missing keys go uncaught.

clusters.summary: Missing blank line before the final `return nil` in IsValid, inconsistent with the spacing of the other blocks in the function.
clusters.rationale: Whitespace preference only.

clusters.summary: Validation is welded into the deserializer itself, unlike every other *FromJSON in the package (and unlike the structural sibling OutgoingWebhookResponse, which has no IsValid at all), so callers lose the ability to parse first and decide about validity separately.
clusters.rationale: Same defect as the maintainer's "let's not throw a hard error, this might break existing servers" comment on that exact return: validation is welded into the decoder so callers cannot parse and then decide, and the fix (move it out of FromJSON) is what the thread asks for.

clusters.summary: The number of ExtraResponses entries is left unbounded even though the new validator walks them all, so a single body under the payload cap can demand thousands of post inserts and websocket broadcasts downstream.
clusters.rationale: No cap on len(ExtraResponses) anywhere, and each entry becomes a post insert plus broadcast; the global 300KB payload cap (server/channels/web/handlers.go:213-216) bounds but does not eliminate the amplification. Pre-existing, and the strict-validation change is the natural place to bound it.

clusters.summary: The new AppError DetailedError strings reaching an untrusted integration caller were examined and cleared, since the web handler calls WipeDetailed whenever EnableDeveloper is off and the strings carry no state or configuration.
clusters.rationale: Cleared note asserting no defect; the clearing checks out — c.Err.WipeDetailed() runs whenever EnableDeveloper is off, and the two new detail strings are static.

clusters.summary: Loop-variable capture in the `for _, resp := range o.ExtraResponses` loop was examined and cleared: the module targets a Go version with per-iteration semantics and no goroutine escapes the loop.
clusters.rationale: Cleared note asserting no defect; the clearing is correct (server/public/go.mod declares go 1.26.3, so loop variables are per-iteration, and nothing escapes the loop).

clusters.summary: Capture of the table-driven test case variable under t.Parallel() was examined and cleared, since the module's Go version gives per-iteration loop variables.
clusters.rationale: Cleared note asserting no defect; correct, since the module targets go 1.26.3 where the range variable is per-iteration.

clusters.summary: Whether the added assert.Error(t, err) duplicates an existing assertion was examined and cleared: the ShouldError branch previously inspected only the nil response and never the error, so the line closes a pre-existing gap.
clusters.rationale: Cleared note asserting no defect; the reading is right — the ShouldError branch previously asserted only assert.Nil(t, response).

clusters.summary: GotoLocation is left unvalidated by the new IsValid, so a malicious slash-command server can set an arbitrary redirect target — cleared because the webapp gates navigation on isUrlSafe.
clusters.rationale: A considered-and-cleared note that asserts no defect; it also reaches the opposite conclusion from thread 4, which wants the URL fields validated more strictly, so it is not a match.

clusters.summary: Attachment text is an unbounded alternate channel around the new Text limit — examined and cleared because attachments remain bounded downstream by PostPropsMaxRunes, so the change opens no new gap.
clusters.rationale: Considered-and-cleared note that asserts no defect introduced by the change.

clusters.summary: A parse failure in the delayed-response endpoint returns 400 before CommandWebhook.TryUse is called, so a retrying integration never consumes one of its five uses and can re-fail indefinitely.
clusters.rationale: Verified ordering: commandWebhook returns 400 on a parse/validation failure before HandleCommandWebhook reaches CommandWebhook().TryUse (server/channels/app/webhook.go:982), so the newly enlarged class of rejected bodies never consumes one of the five uses. Real but low impact.
